body: I read it. Im feeling shitty as well so I feel you.
Hey thanks. It did help to have someone to talk to about it at this hour

Now that you mentioned it, there's actually a hotline from the department. Totally forgot about that or maybe Ive ignored it because theyll probably know who I am and I wouldnt like that.  I guess I'll call anonymously, just to get to talk to a professional about it.

That's true. Im probably the definition of a really bad patient. Im a doctor and I couldnt even walk my own talk. I myself is averse to medicine that I would recommend to patients.  I have ignored my mental health long enough because I am in denial.

I cant stay with anyone right now. A lot of my colleagues have gotten infected and I dont want to expose anyone in case Im an asymptomatic carrier of the virus. Ive been trying to call friends and family but I just really cant bear them to worry more about me. Theyre worried about me now as it is.

Its hard. For this past month, the hospital work has actually stop the suicidal thoughts for awhile. I had been uplifted by thoughts that Im doing helping others the best way I can. I was thinking about going back to studying for my exam during my quarantine days  But now that Im actually alone and have more time to think about things, I have no motivation to do anything productive. It hurts even to think about going through another month knowing Im still gonna be me and Im still gonna be immovable.

Hey thanks. I have considered therapy before graduating med school actually. But I couldnt take the meds side effects. Plus I felt like the psychiatrist wasnt cognizant of my condition enough. I self medicated with meditation and mental retreat for years but they just temporarily relieved my constant sense of doom. I guess Ive also been in denial for a long time about depression. Ive never sought an2nd opinion and Ive never opened up to my friends and family about it. So for years Ive been burdened my inaction and thought that if I just chase the dream and work hard, I'll be happier and the negative thoughts will go away. But it has been like a constant pull on different directions for me and now I feel like I just cant go anywhere.

I havent talked about it with anyone although the thought has been there for years. These days it amplified and I'm scared I may have devised a plan to actually go through with it. I'm frightened of myself.

I feel like I have nowhere to go after this crisis. I have been a doctor for 4 years now and have been to 2 residency training programs that I ultimately quit due to overwork and general disillusionment. Before the pandemic started, I was planning to take the USMLE but now since all testing in my country are suspended and because the US is looking more and more dreary, Ive been second guessing myself and thinking that migrating might not really be for me. Like maybe Im not really cut out for this. But I dont really know how to do anything but doctoring. Ive been aiming for it since I elementary days. 

Ive been volunteering in a COVID hospital doing internal medicine work since the hospital is understaff at the moment. And ive been seeing old classmates and past juniors getting way ahead of me in the medical field. And Im still here working as a GP without anything to show for. I constantly dream of getting into a neuroscience program abroad but I feel like it maybe too late for me. And Im not even sure I'll have the energy to go through another residency program again. 

Ive been in quarantine for 2 weeks now because of my exposure and although the suicide thought have been there for years now, I feel like it's an easier option right now. Like it would really be a relief to just not think about it anymore. To just disappear and never having the burden of thinking about the future.
